hypotheses.reasoning: audit.events partition 2 consumer is stuck on msg-440333 (offset 836959). Its payload contains a NUL byte at position 1323, so JSON parsing fails on every attempt. The consumer nacks and redelivers with no max-retry limit (attempt 4 at 07:54:01, attempt 13 by 07:55:25), so the partition head never advances. Lag then grows steadily from 858 messages at 07:57 to about 6400 by 08:06 (lines 2258, 2336, 2474, 2678, 3109, 3286). CPU is normal because the consumer is blocked on retries, not computing. The notification-svc v1.9.0 TypeError, the api-gateway 500s, the account-svc timeouts and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts are separate, unrelated symptoms and do not explain the audit lag.

The alternative reading is that the NUL byte is corrupt data written upstream into the audit record, which would make it a data_integrity problem at the producer. The logs do not show the producer, so the origin of the corruption is unconfirmed. The fix (skip or dead-letter the message) is the same either way.

verdict.recommendedAction: Dead-letter or skip msg-440333 (audit.events partition 2, offset 836959) so the consumer can advance, then drain the roughly 6400-message backlog. Add a max-retry limit with a dead-letter queue to audit-consumer so one bad payload cannot block a partition again. Trace where the NUL byte was written upstream and add input validation at the producer. Separately, the notification-svc v1.9.0 'currency' TypeError (lines 2077, 2188) and the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts (2005) need their own follow-up, though they do not drive this alert.
